messages:
marie: Heads up — since ~09:17 we've been seeing large tail latency on multi-GPU jobs in us-west2. NCCL all-reduce times jumped ~4x, throughput dropped, and a few jobs hit NCCL TIMEOUTs. Not CPU or GPU bound.
akshay: Any recent infra changes in us-west2? config, kernel, or firmware rolls?
marie: No infra deploys in last 24h. I see pattern across several racks/TORs though — jobs pinned to different ToRs show similar symptoms.
jon: Can you paste a short nccl-tests output and one of the pod's dmesg/syslog? quick grep for TIMEOUTs
marie: paste:

"""
# ./all_reduce_perf -b 8 -e 512M -f 2 -g 8
# nRanks 8 nGpus 8 minBytes 8 maxBytes 536870912 step: 2
# out-of-place warmup iters: 5 iters: 10
# size  bytes #bytes / rank  time (usec)  algbw  busbw  error
33554432    33554432    5    12345.67    2.7    21.3   0
67108864    67108864    5    49800.12    0.67   5.3    0

# NCCL WARN TIMEOUT
"""

and node dmesg shows repeated mlx5 warnings:

"""
mlx5_core 0000:81:00.0 eth0: port 1 MCA overflow
mlx5_core 0000:81:00.0 eth0: rx buffer drop
"""

lina: MCA overflow / rx drops smell like bufferbloat / queue scheduling issues on the ToR. Any change to QoS profiles or TC rules?
akshay: Checking cloud config — no tc changes. But I noticed a kube-proxy DaemonSet update last week that bumped conntrack config and sysctl changes; could interact with kernel networking buffer usage.
marie: I grabbed ethtool and mlx5 counters from one affected host:

"""
# ethtool -S eth0 | head
rx_packets: 12345678
rx_dropped: 1200
rx_missed_errors: 0

# cat /sys/class/infiniband/mlx5_0/ports/1/counters/rx_packets
...
# mlx5_core stats show high rx_drop due to MCA
"""

jon: Any MTU mismatches? RoCE is sensitive. Also check switch-level pause frames / PFC config and if ECN/RED changed.
lina: I ran mtu check across the pod hosts and ToR: most are 9000 but two leaf switches still had 1500 on one VLAN after a config drift during maintenance. I flagged it earlier but it didn't affect unidirectional heavy flows until today.
marie: Interesting — flows are east-west and bi-directional. When flows traverse that 1500 segment we get lots of segmentation and reassembly, which can cause bursts and buffer exhaustion.
jon: That plus any AQM (RED/CoDel) misconfig could create sawtooth throughput and long tails. Can you run a TCP/UDP iperf test and an RDMA read/write microbench between two GPUs that are topologically separated across the mismatched switch?
marie: iperf3 UDP test (one-direction) shows ~80% goodput with 1–2% loss and huge jitter spikes. RDMA bandwidth (ib_write_bw) shows inconsistent numbers with occasional <10% of expected.

sre-bot: NOTICE: rack-12 ToR config drift detected — VLAN 430 MTU=1500 (expected 9000). Ticket INC-10234 opened.
deploy-bot: autopruned: rolled back a recent leaf firmware on 2026-03-17 02:12 UTC to previous stable — change note: none that should affect MTU.

akshay: OK let's do a plan:
1) Quarantine affected VLAN (route traffic away) or add explicit MTU/fragmentation path to avoid mixed MTU inside NCCL jobs.
2) Temporarily schedule NCCL jobs to same ToR (reduce east-west) while we fix MTU.
3) Collect dump of switch buffer occupancy (counters) during a repro run, plus per-host mlx5 stats.

lina: I've applied a config fix to the ToR and set MTU=9000 on VLAN 430. Pushing to other affected ToRs now. Will monitor.
marie: After fix, reran same all_reduce_perf: time dropped from 49800 usec to 13600 usec on that size. No more NCCL TIMEOUTs for the test job.
jon: Nice. Still want to capture why we didn't see this earlier: maybe a recent bump in job size or change in routing exposed the path. Also, look into switch buffer sizing and possible PFC misconfig — if PFC was disabled we might mask drops but increase latency.
akshay: We should add an automated MTU/Path check in our scheduler pre-flight for multi-gpu jobs: verify path MTU and RDMA compatibility. If mismatch, warn and autoschedule intra-rack only.
marie: Agreed. Filing follow-up RFC: 1) scheduler path MTU check 2) infra alerting on VLAN MTU deviations 3) runbook for quick quarantine. I'll attach logs/timestamps to INC-10234.
lina: Also we should check firmware on those ToRs — I saw a minor change recently that changed jumbo handling defaults. Pushing a ticket to network team.

jon: Quick note for postmortem — actionable items:
- scheduler path MTU check
- add RDMA/ibverbs-specific health probe in our CI stress tests
- baseline switch buffer occupancy metrics + alert on MCA overflow
- make NCCL jobs default to intra-rack placement unless override

marie: Thanks all. For now, jobs are green in us-west2 after MTU fix. Will keep monitoring for 24h. :thumbsup:
akshay: Nice catch Lina. Great teamwork. :party_parrot:
